topic: Actuated-nib pen that scribes predefined characters (BIC)
citation: BIC Violex Single Member S.A. (inventors Polygerinos P., Chrysanthakopoulos N.). Writing instrument. US 12,026,327 B2, granted 2024-07-02; appl. US 18/187,156 filed 2023-03-21; pre-grant pub. US 2023/0305647 A1 (2023-09-28); priority EP 22164386.9 (2022-03-25). Family: EP 4250070 A1. Status: Active, anticipated expiration 2043-03-21 (as displayed on Google Patents on 2026-09-26; not verified in official register).
task_or_setup: Handheld pen: elongate body; electronically actuated nib manipulator at the proximal (writing) end moving the nib end portion in XP/YP (plane substantially orthogonal to the pen axis) and ZP (along the axis); IMU measuring the position (orientation) of the principal axis relative to the writing surface; ECU executing segment formation commands (from speech, image or text input) to scribe predefined characters. Embodiment: 3-arm delta/parallel mechanism (carbon-fibre or Kevlar arms; Kapton flexure joints) driven by linear actuators via rods/push-pull cables, or motors winding wire linkages, or piezoelectric strips laminated at the flexible joints; optional actuator position feedback or end-of-limit switches; tracking wheel/trackball/optical displacement detector on a protrusion; contact detector (microswitch, compressible seat, or actuator resistance sensing); ink fed by flexible tube.
participants_or_bench: None (no prototype test data disclosed)
comparator: References cited on face include US 4,211,012 A; US 5,501,535 A; US 5,861,877 A; US 2015/0148948 A1; US 2020/0202741 A1; CN 109263362 A; JP 2006211497 A; KR 20090005210 A; NPL Speech Pen (CHI 2006), Pentelligence (2018).
key_quantitative_findings: 20 claims. Independent: cl. 1 writing instrument (body defining principal axis A; electronically actuated nib manipulator moving nib end portion within a spatial domain along first XP and second YP axes of a plane substantially orthogonal to A and along a third ZP axis; IMU measuring at least a position of A relative to a writing surface; ECU obtaining segment formation commands, receiving axis position from IMU and actuating the manipulator to scribe a predefined character defined by the commands); cl. 15 computer-implemented method (audio or graphical sample -> speech/image recognition -> character identifiers -> predefined character store records -> segment formation commands provided to the pen); cl. 18 system (pen + external processing apparatus + wireless network; external speech recognition and character store). Cl. 16-17 program element/medium referring to cl. 15. Dependent: 2 robotic mechanism with plural arms; 3 arm proximal ends coupled to end portion, distal ends to actuators; 4 delta mechanism; 5 prevents rotation about A; 6 displacement detector (velocity across surface) used in actuation; 7 detector on a protrusion = trackball, encoder tracking wheel, or optical sensor contacting the surface; 8 contact detector triggers scribing; 9-13 microphone, audio processing, modem, speech recognition, character store; 14 ink supply + flexible tube, or pencil/crayon; 19-20 system with the claim-1 pen. Disclosed numbers: body length 50-200 mm (example 140 mm); max diameter 6-25 mm (example 15 mm); axis-to-surface angles 80/70/60/50/45 deg compensated via ZP; 3 DOF.
units_and_conditions: mm; degrees. No speed, accuracy, force or bandwidth values disclosed.
locator: Claims 1-20 (cols. 21-24); description cols. 4-13 (nib manipulator, IMU, ECU, delta mechanism, piezo strips, displacement detector, contact detector); front page.
limitations: Claims transcribed from OCR of the official USPTO image PDF with obvious OCR artefacts corrected; verify against a certified copy. Status/expiry as displayed on Google Patents on 2026-09-26; not verified in official register. Continuations/divisionals not checked. The description never mentions tremor. Not a legal opinion.
relevance_to_design: Closest granted claim found. Claim 1 recites (a) nib moved relative to the body in XP/YP plus ZP by an electronically actuated manipulator with an IMU and ECU, and (g) scribing predefined characters from commands; dependent claims touch (c) an optical displacement sensor on a protrusion, contact detection (e, binary), and arms driven by actuators at their distal (rear) ends (cf. j).
transferability_reason: Same product class and architecture (handheld pen, nib actuated relative to barrel, IMU, controller); purpose differs (autonomous scribing of commanded characters, not tremor cancellation or user-led bounded guidance).
design_implication: Treat as the primary FTO reference for any guided-letter mode that moves the nib to form predefined characters. Record design choices (2-axis stage without active ZP, user-led motion with bounded local correction, how target shapes are represented) for attorney review of the 'spatial domain ... (ii) along a third (ZP) axis' and 'segment formation commands' limitations.

topic: Anti-tremor pen with X-Y actuated refill guidance ('vector force guidance')
citation: Shaoyang Industrial Vocational and Technical College (inventors Liu Pan, Liu Fei, Li Bing, Lyu Fa, Zhou Yuan, Ouyang Jianfeng, Liu Yuanzhi, Mao Yi, Zhong Meixing, Cao Xuan). Smart anti-shake pen and writing method based on vector force guidance [基于矢量力引导的智能防抖笔及书写方法]. CN 121979402 A, published 2026-05-05; appl. CN 202610221299.6 filed 2026-02-24 (priority date 2026-02-24). Status: Pending (as displayed on Google Patents on 2026-09-26; not verified in official register; not checked at CNIPA).
task_or_setup: Pen shell with inner core support; refill in a refill sleeve, slidable along the pen axis; tremor suppression module = IMU + 'reverse micro-vibration assemblies' (micro vibration motor + eccentric mass) generating a compensation moment on the pen body; vector-force stroke module = at least two orthogonal linear micro-drivers (voice coil or piezoceramic) pushing, via hinged push rods, a guide ring fixed on the refill sleeve that translates in an X-Y plane perpendicular to the pen axis; nib pressure sensor; miniature image sensor with wide-angle lens and inclined illumination at the nib; Bluetooth/Wi-Fi link to a terminal that issues stroke vectors and compares returned trajectories.
participants_or_bench: None (patent disclosure; no test data reported)
key_quantitative_findings: 10 claims (machine translation). Cl. 1 device: shell, inner core support, refill assembly, tremor suppression module (IMU on the core support monitoring angular velocity and linear acceleration; reverse micro-vibration assemblies each = micro vibration motor + eccentric mass), vector-force stroke auxiliary drive module, bidirectional interaction module, main controller coordinating tremor suppression and guidance. Cl. 3 controllable guidance force on the refill sleeve in the 2-D writing plane per external command. Cl. 5 inverse-dynamics model computes a compensation moment opposite to the current tremor trend; motors driven at specific speed and phase. Cl. 6 >=2 mutually orthogonal linear micro-drivers define an X-Y frame perpendicular to the pen axis; stroke vector command decomposed into X/Y components to synthesise a resultant force guiding the refill along a preset stroke track. Cl. 7 guide ring + guide rail constrain motion to pure translation, preventing refill inclination. Cl. 8 voice-coil or piezoceramic actuators; hinged push rods. Cl. 9 axial nib pressure sensor between refill tail and sleeve; miniature camera at the nib; digital image correlation or feature-point tracking gives the pen motion vector, combined with pen geometry to compute the nib trajectory. Cl. 10 method: A init; target font decomposed into ordered strokes (start point, direction vector, length, recommended speed); B issue stroke vector; C1 high-priority anti-tremor thread + C2 guidance thread; D trajectory and pressure streamed back; E similarity comparison with completion threshold or time limit, then next stroke. Numbers: IMU sampled at 'hundreds of hertz' (description, per machine translation); no force, stroke or bandwidth values found.
units_and_conditions: Hz (qualitative only). Machine translation of Chinese text.
locator: Claims 1-10; abstract; description (machine translation on Google Patents).
limitations: Machine translation is garbled in places (e.g., 'anti-curlicue' for the pen); check claim wording against the Chinese original. Unexamined application: claims may be amended. Priority 2026-02-24; prior-art effect depends on our own filing dates; PCT/foreign filings still possible until 2027-02-24. Status as displayed on Google Patents on 2026-09-26; not verified in official register. Not a legal opinion.
relevance_to_design: Closest overall combination found: tremor handling + 2-axis actuated refill relative to the barrel (a) + IMU tremor sensing (b) + camera at the nib (c) + nib force sensor (e) + guided strokes along target characters (g) + trajectory capture/comparison (i). Tremor is countered by eccentric-mass counter-moment on the whole pen, not by nib displacement; refill is constrained to translation (no pivot).
transferability_reason: Same product class, sensor set and guidance function; mechanism differs (translating guide ring with orthogonal linear drivers vs our flexure/pivot stage; eccentric-mass tremor suppression vs nib-displacement cancellation).
design_implication: Monitor CNIPA prosecution and any PCT/foreign equivalents (window to 2027-02-24). Ask attorney whether nib-displacement tremor cancellation without eccentric-mass motors and a pivoting (tilting) refill stay outside claim 1 as it may be amended. Cite as prior art for guided strokes + nib-camera tracking in our own filings.

topic: Tremor-filtered handwriting redrawn by an actuated pen carriage (Verily)
citation: Verily Life Sciences LLC (inventors Pathak A., Allen M.). Apparatus, system, and method to stabilize penmanship and reduce tremor. US 10,101,824 B2, granted 2018-10-16; appl. US 15/220,905 filed 2016-07-27 (priority 2016-07-27); also US 2018/0032159 A1, WO 2018/022356 A1. Status: Active, expires 2036-10-13 (as displayed on Google Patents on 2026-09-26; not verified in official register).
task_or_setup: Portable writing stage whose writing-instrument carriage is moved by an actuator system (at least two independent stepper motors with miniature lead screws for X/Y; Z motion to engage/disengage) with a pressure sensor; a stylus (or touch screen) captures the user's tremulous handwriting; a processing apparatus filters tremor (low-pass, notch, adaptive/user-specific, machine learning) and may down-scale; the stage re-draws the filtered characters with pressure regulation; optional optical sensor examines the drawn line.
participants_or_bench: None (patent disclosure; no test data reported)
key_quantitative_findings: 22 claims. Cl. 1 portable writing apparatus: writing-instrument carriage (removable, interchangeable instruments); actuator system moving the carriage; pressure sensor system measuring pressure applied by the writing instrument; controller receiving input data describing a user's handwritten characters, moving the carriage so it recreates their shape, measuring pressure while doing so and adjusting the pressure applied by the actuator system. Dependent: 2 input filtered to remove tremor data; 3 scaled to reduce size; 4 controller filters and scales; 5 motion orthogonal to the 2-D plane to engage/disengage; 6 at least two independent stepper motors; 7 clamps/screw structure; 8 optical sensor examines a line drawn and pressure is adjusted. Cl. 9 system: portable writing stage (as cl. 1) + stylus outputting handwriting data + processing apparatus filtering tremor data and sending filtered data that makes the carriage recreate the characters. Cl. 14 method of tremor reduction: receive stylus movement data; filter tremor; send to a mechanical stage with mobile and immobile segments; trace filtered shapes; determine and adjust writing pressure. Dependent 15-22: 2-D mobile segment holding pen/pencil; lift between characters; pen form-factor stylus; down-scaling; adaptive filtering storing user-specific tremor parameters (19) with machine learning (22); low-pass or notch filtering (20); stylus or apparatus motion tracking (21). No numeric performance values in claims.
locator: Claims 1-22 (USPTO PDF pp. 12-13 of 13); description (stepper motors, lead screws, filters).
limitations: Claims transcribed from OCR of the official USPTO image PDF; verify against a certified copy. Status/expiry as displayed on Google Patents on 2026-09-26; not verified in official register. Separate stylus and stage, not a single handheld pen. Not a legal opinion.
relevance_to_design: Claims recite contact-force measurement and regulation (e) on an actuated writing-instrument carriage, tremor filtering of captured handwriting (b-related, sensor-agnostic) with adaptive user-specific parameters, redrawing the filtered (corrected) shapes (i-related), and optical inspection of the drawn line (cl. 8).
transferability_reason: Same problem (tremor-free handwriting via actuated writing instrument with pressure control); architecture differs (off-line stylus capture + separate portable stage vs a single handheld pen that corrects in real time).
design_implication: Active until 2036 as displayed: attorney to assess whether a handheld pen whose refill carriage is moved by actuators, with nib force regulation and on-board tremor filtering, could be a 'portable writing apparatus' that 'recreates a shape of the user's handwritten characters' (cl. 1) or performs the cl. 14 method; avoid relying on 'adjusting the pressure applied by the actuator system' unless cleared.
